I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

    According to recent reports, there’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

    In a recent development, there will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

    Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

    If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

    Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

    Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the significant spenders.

    Recent findings suggest that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s upcoming leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    It has been revealed that brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

    Nvidia surge: What investors should do with the stock and the AI trade now

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.
    • Investors and traders noted that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the organization and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • Sources indicate that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders noted that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the organization and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    Sources indicate that "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," mentioned Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same concerns that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    The day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    It has been revealed that mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also said there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    Jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he stated, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    It has been revealed that the national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    In a recent development, "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the firm's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) said in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    Industry observers note that house Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the manufacturer does so much international business.

    Recent findings suggest that "This is an export control problem," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong issue for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," mentioned Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    In a recent development, to be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic upcoming look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

    The Manchester City striker revealed his upcoming buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

    Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

    In a recent development, pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

    Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

    Industry observers note that haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a newly introduced campaign.

    It is a latest-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

    Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

    So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

    “I’ll try to find a fresh Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many notable things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

    It has been revealed that “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

    “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

    It has been revealed that maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

    “But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

    “The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

    “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

    #107841. Industry News: Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (754 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (754 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.
    • But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.
    • Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kalshi is known for its prediction markets across sports, politics and culture.

    But now, for the first time, perpetual futures, Kalshi's second financial product, has surpassed the notional trading volume of its event contracts on consecutive days.

    Sources indicate that on Thursday, perpetual futures — commonly known as "perps" — on Kalshi saw $3.4 billion in notional volume as artificial intelligence laboratory Anthropic stock debuted on public markets while the rest of the market sold off. That exceeded about $3 billion in notional volume for Kalshi's prediction markets on the same day.

    Perps are futures-style contracts where there is no expiration and traders do not need to own the underlying asset. Contracts instead continuously track the price of an asset, with funding payments to keep the contract price aligned with that of the market. Funding payments are made periodically between holders of short or long positions.

    Sources indicate that perps trading surpassed event contracts one day in September, but on Friday perps topped prediction markets volume for a second day. Now Kalshi expects that performance to continue as it introduces perps tied to more individual stocks. On Monday, for example, Kalshi launched contracts linked to Anthropic.

    Recent findings suggest that kalshi was the first to debut perps in the U.S. after winning federal regulatory approval in May to list perps tied to cryptocurrencies.

    Perps trading volume includes any leverage that speculators acquire along with their trade, while event contracts are fully collateralized — for now.

    Since the original launch in May, Kalshi has received approval to introduce perps tied to metals, crude oil, stock indexes and individual stocks.

    Sources indicate that offshore perps — those available on exchanges not regulated in the U.S. — generated more than $90 trillion in notional trading volume in 2025, so it's not surprising that the product has grown so rapidly on Kalshi, according to Udesh Jha, chief risk officer at Kalshi Klear, the company's clearing house.

    "We're just in very early innings. We're launching products, we're growing the participant base.".

    Perps were Kalshi's first product to mark its transition from a prediction market-focused platform to a full-blown financial exchange where various assets are traded. Last week, reports stated that Kalshi is planning to offer trading on equities on its platform in the coming months.

    At the same time, the company's perps product has come under fire. Some incumbent exchanges where futures are traded — which saw their stock prices decline following the approval of U.S. perps — believe the product was improperly approved. CME Group is suing the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal derivatives regulator, for approving perps.

    Others have simply expressed concerns about the efficiency of the markets. CNBC previously reported that trading volume on Kalshi's most popular perps markets — tied to bitcoin and ether cryptocurrencies — was dramatically greater than open interest, or cash actively in the markets. It's a phenomenon that isn't common with U.S.-regulated traditional futures, nor other offshore perps markets.

    Kalshi stated at the time it has "zero concerns" about the distinction, and that it appears because less leverage is offered compared to offshore exchanges and there are fewer incentives for traders to park capital on its perps markets.

    While Kalshi started with cryptocurrencies, Owen Lau, an analyst at Clear Street, remarked perps tied to individual stocks likely represent the most promising opportunity for growth in the U.S.

    Recent findings suggest that "That's how I foresee the way perps will penetrate further into traditional asset classes," Lau mentioned. "Perps on single stocks and [key performance indicators on individual companies] could change how investors hedge their portfolio or even make a directional bet.".

    Kalshi's growth has been powered by the fact that right now it's the only exchange that can actively list perps in the U.S., though crypto exchange Coinbase received approval in May to route U.S. users to offshore platforms for trading. That monopoly status, however, will probably prove short lived.

    Coinbase has filed to list single-stock perps in the U.S., and President Donald Trump in August noted the CFTC is working to bring Hyperliquid — a dominant player in offshore perps activity — to domestic traders.

    But Jha at Kalshi isn't worried about the competition.

    According to recent reports, "What will carry us is ... making sure that we have the right products for the marketplace, making sure we have the right surveillance of the products that we are trading.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    AI debt markets shudder as Nvidia's top 'banker' returns

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.
    • Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.
    • In a recent development, huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    AI credit markets are shuddering again with Jensen Huang back as CEO of Nvidia.

    Fears about the massive debt being taken on to fund the artificial intelligence buildout climbed Tuesday as Wall Street weighed what Huang's return to Nvidia means for its bankrolling of the AI boom.

    In a recent development, huang is considered one of the top financiers, or bankers, in the AI industry, spearheading deals with neoclouds like CoreWeave and other firms to buy chips, backed in some cases by Nvidia guarantees. His return to Nvidia has revived prospects for the company to continue "circular financing" of AI chips and data centers — raising concerns among credit investors.

    Industry observers note that coreWeave, which has become the poster child of AI debt concerns, saw its stock sink 13% and the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 top 17%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    According to recent reports, at the same time, the spread on the neocloud organization's five-year credit default swaps jumped 8.5% to over 1,200 basis points. Credit default swaps are insurance against nonpayment and are considered a barometer of perceived risks. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.

    Huang was reinstated as CEO on Monday after stepping down on Nov. 12 amid allegations of multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. His reinstatement on Monday was cheered by investors, who pushed stocks higher, yields lower and spreads on CDS tighter. However, stocks retreated, bond yields rose and CDS spreads widened on Tuesday.

    Ben Emons, founder and chief investment officer at FedWatch Advisors, called it a waning of the "Jensen effect.".

    The moves suggest "markets see government intervention as 'moral suasion' that carries credit and interest-rate risks," he stated.

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday he "convinced" the board to bring Huang back.

    It has been revealed that coreWeave wasn't the only name seeing heightened concerns in CDS spreads. Oracle's five-year CDS spread jumped 7% to 355.68. Even highly rated hyperscalers Meta Platforms and Amazon.com saw spreads widen by more than 2%. Nvidia's CDS added 3.4%.

    Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds, believes the drama that unfolded with Huang's return to Nvidia won't necessarily sit well with credit investors.

    According to recent reports, "A lot of old school credit people are going to look at what kind of materialized there, the administration's involvement in putting him back in, and I think a lot of credit participants are going to step back and tiptoe away from that a bit," he stated. "Credit market investors typically don't like that type of drama or uncertainty.".

    It has been revealed that while Nvidia has commitments across the AI ecosystem, it is the neoclouds that have been under the most scrutiny. Many of the companies, which rent out AI computing power and cloud capacity, are highly leveraged and have relied on Nvidia financing to reduce their exposure to the bond market.

    With so much riding on Nvidia's funding, Huang's next move is being closely watched.

    During his brief absence, chief financial officer Colette Kress said during the manufacturer's earnings call that Nvidia would be "rigorously evaluating future investments" and will remain disciplined in how it commits capital.

    That suggested Nvidia was going to be more judicious with financing, says Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets.

    "That concern should be put to rest with Jensen [Huang] back," he said.

    Investor Steve Eisman, of "Massive Short" fame and host of "The Real Eisman Playbook" podcast, believes Huang feels emboldened now that he's back in charge.

    "[H]e'll double down on the circular financing," Eisman predicted on CNBC's "Squawk Box" Tuesday.

    After Huang's departure, Eisman believed that the ecosystem the CEO created by pouring money into AI companies would likely unwind and leave some of the companies in "substantial trouble.".

    "Now that he's back, they're not," he noted.

    Others are not so certain the level of funding will continue.

    "Given scrutiny of disclosure around financing and guarantees … we do not expect Mr. Huang's return to bring a quick reversion to broader customer financing," Stifel analyst Ruben Roy remarked in a note Monday.

    In a recent development, nvidia stated on its earnings call that it has $118 billion in guarantees, as of Oct. 25, to back AI projects.

    Concerns about the level of debt to fund the AI infrastructure buildout had already taken hold before Huang's departure and reinstatement.

    "These complications have not disappeared just because the White House pressured the weak board to reinstate Jensen Huang," stated economist David Rosenberg, founder and president of Rosenberg Research.

    John Lloyd, global head of multi-sector and corporate credit at Janus Henderson Investors, believes having Huang back at the helm "reaffirms his existing go-to-market strategy." However, the credit market is still taking a cautious look at the neoclouds as it waits for more clarity on long-term supply/demand dynamics.

    Still, Lloyd is cautiously positive on CoreWeave, which he owns in portfolios he manages, and noted all the data point to a "pretty healthy environment right now." That includes strong residual values on graphics processing units and spot compute rates, he noted.

    "The company is doing everything in its power to execute," he remarked. "They don't need the high yield market at this time.".

    In the meantime, investigations into Nvidia and Huang are ramping up. Huang is expected to appear before three House committees next week. Nvidia is conducting an independent investigation into his activities, and California Attorney General Rob Bonta has rolled out a probe. At the federal level, President Trump said Monday that U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche "has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    Sources indicate that "There's other shoes to drop," Rosenberg said. "I don't think that the book has been closed on this file.".

    #107829. Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (979 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Nvidia's billion-dollar board bet: Who's protected as lawsuits mount?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the company's board to rehire Huang.
    • Recent findings suggest that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-tech giant director.
    • California Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia, after President Donald Trump urged the company's board to rehire Huang. But the investigation into the company, its executive leadership and its board continue as outside criticism mounts.

    Recent findings suggest that "Clearly they caved to external pressure," stated Betsy Atkins, an author and longtime public-tech giant director. "The board failed," she said, when it initially allowed Huang's removal. "The board's role is to think of all stakeholders.".

    California Attorney General Rob Bonta is investigating whether Nvidia misrepresented information to investors. "There is classic corporate securities law on the books in California that prevents investors and the public from being misled by companies," Bonta said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday.

    Directors are already defendants in a shareholder lawsuit accusing them of failing to oversee Nvidia. A separate securities class action targets the organization and Huang, its co-founder.

    Recent findings suggest that now the board’s insurance choices are part of the story. A risk advisor with direct knowledge of Nvidia’s coverage notes the firm built an approximately $1 billion D&O tower, insurance jargon for directors and officers insurance policies from different companies that combine to cover one massive risk.

    Industry observers note that nvidia "loves insurance," the advisor said. “They buy insurance as if they have no balance sheet.” A billion-dollar tower would essentially mean Nvidia "bought the market," purchasing all the coverage it could get, according to an industry expert with 25 years working in financial insurance. The expert asked not to be named out of concern for past or potential future clients.

    Recent findings suggest that but Nvidia directed all that coverage to Side A only, according to CNBC's source, which protects directors and officers personally when the company cannot indemnify them. Side B and C leaves Nvidia to bear more of its own risk and legal costs. The risk advisor says Nvidia believed it had "the war chest" to protect itself against a securities class action suit.

    That choice is raising questions about whether the board protected itself at the tech giant’s expense. CNBC asked Nvidia for comment but received no response.

    An insurance CEO characterized a billion dollar policy as a lot of coverage, but remarked a Side A-only allocation was a surprising move because it results in imbalanced coverage, protecting only directors.

    In a recent development, that structure is not automatically a governance failure, according to a D&O insurance expert with long experience in coverage for banks, drugmakers and other businesses that often face litigation. Side A-only programs are common among companies with the capital to manage the corporate risk internally.

    In a recent development, "For a organization with Nvidia’s resources, retaining the company-side risk can make financial sense," the adviser noted. It's Side A D&O that's "imperative to corporate governance.".

    "It is a capital-allocation decision," the expert told me. The company decides that buying insurance for its own balance sheet is not worth the premium. In other words, Side B, which covers the company for legal defense costs or settlements on behalf of directors and officers, and Side C, protecting the company when named as a defendant in a suit such as a securities claim, are considered too expensive for the coverage the company gets.

    The question for shareholders is whether the board’s decision to hold that risk was a sound use of the manufacturer’s resources and whether the company can absorb the costs if the claims grow.

    Sources indicate that A shareholder derivative complaint filed Nov. 11 names Huang, directors and other officers. It alleges that they failed to oversee risks involving Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and made misleading statements. It also alleges that some defendants sold roughly $2 billion in Nvidia stock while holding material nonpublic information. Those remain allegations, not findings.

    A separate securities class action, filed Nov. 9, names Nvidia and Huang. It seeks damages for investors who bought Nvidia shares between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, alleging the manufacturer and Huang misled investors. The distinction matters: the derivative suit is brought on Nvidia’s behalf, while the class action seeks recovery for investors.

    "Insurance is already at work," says Michel Léonard, chief economist at the Insurance Information Institute, describing standard policy mechanics, not Nvidia’s specific policy. "Once the suit is filed, D&O starts paying defense costs, long before anyone proves anything.".

    Recent findings suggest that A claim still has to meet the policy’s terms, and defense costs can reduce the remaining limits. Nor does a drop in Nvidia’s market value by itself establish an insurable loss. Plaintiffs would need to prove legally recoverable damages; the policy would respond only to covered losses.

    According to recent reports, the board has already taken steps it notes are aimed at accountability. Nvidia announced an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and independent directors retained outside counsel two days later. Huang resigned as CEO and a director on Nov. 11; the board appointed CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. Nvidia remarked it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised by Huang's extramarital relationships.

    In a recent development, atkins, who joined the board of Wynn Resorts in 2018 after founder Steve Wynn resigned, argues that allegations are not conclusions and that boards should also weigh governance concerns against the value a founder brings to a organization’s innovation. Nvidia's investigation is continuing even as Huang resumes leadership.

    Sources indicate that “Will companies’ hyper-accelerated innovation speed be the same without them? I don’t think so,” noted Atkins, author of Don't Waste a Board Seat: A Decision-Maker's Guide to Choosing Directors Who Create Value.

    Nvidia’s 2026 proxy also states the manufacturer has indemnity agreements with its directors and officers — separate from its insurance. Those agreements provide for the company to cover certain costs and liabilities when the law permits.

    • In a recent development, we're onto Week 6!
    • It has been revealed that ausar is averaging 10.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals and 1 block on 55% shooting through 16 games, and he's been even better lately.
    • Industry observers note that I have him 57th, as I anticipate Jalen Duren's return will impact his numbers to some degree.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, we're onto Week 6! Here is the 9-cat version of my risers and fallers list. These rankings are for rest-of-season 9-cat leagues, and I'm leaning on Yahoo's rankings from the last two weeks and last month. Efficiency matters more here than in points leagues, and it's the main thing separating these six players. Let's get into it!

    It has been revealed that ausar is averaging 10.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 5.4 assists, 1.6 steals and 1 block on 55% shooting through 16 games, and he's been even better lately. He's eighth over the last two weeks and 30th over the last month. He leads the Pistons in rebounding and had a 17-board game against Philadelphia on Nov. 4. The weak spots are well known. Those with punt-3 builds get the most out of him, since he positively adds value in rebounds, assists, stocks and field goal percentage. The jump to 73% from the line is another win, as he doesn't hurt you nearly as badly as he used to.

    Industry observers note that I have him 57th, as I anticipate Jalen Duren's return will impact his numbers to some degree. Either way, he's exceeding expectations in what could be a breakout campaign.

    Smith is averaging 14.1 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.1 3s and 1 block in 25.3 minutes, shooting 55% from the field with 0.9 turnovers per game. That mix of 3s, blocks, field goal percentage and low turnovers is why he grades out well in 9-cat without much volume. He's 14th over the last two weeks and 26th over the last month. He was drafted in just 8% of Yahoo leagues, so if you scooped him up off waivers, you're playing with house money.

    I'm moving him up to 65th, from 99th, but not higher because much of this production came with Nic Claxton sidelined. Caleb Wilson is also out, and Claxton is still ramping up, so Smith's role should hold for now. I could be too low on him. Continue to hold.

    McDaniels is 11th over the last two weeks and 18th over the last month. The bump in usage comes from Anthony Edwards' absence. Edwards is out until late January after knee surgery, and McDaniels has absorbed a bigger share of the offense without losing efficiency. He's averaging 18.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.2 steals, 0.9 blocks and 1.6 3s in 33.9 minutes, shooting 56% from the field and 85% from the line.

    Recent findings suggest that he's positive in eight of nine categories, with turnovers (2.2 per game) the only negative. I don't value turnovers that much, especially when he's so productive across other areas of fantasy. Some of that scoring should come back down when Edwards returns, which is why I have him 30th, up from 43rd. I wouldn't sell, even though his play is on another level right now.

    In a recent development, hart is 233rd over the last two weeks and 176th over the last month. His scoring is down to 6.6 points per game from 12.0 last season, and he's shooting 34% from the field and 60% from the line. He's still contributing 6.7 rebounds and 4.0 assists, which keeps him rosterable, but his steals have dipped recently and he's listed as questionable with a right shoulder sprain. In 9-cat, the low percentages make it a bigger problem. The good news is that his minutes appear to be trending back up. Landry Shamet's been eating into his minutes because of his shooting, but over the past two games, Hart's averaging 37 minutes per gam. He's also coming off a 10-11-10 triple-double, which could be a nice selling point if you're concerned about his ROS outlook.

    Industry observers note that I have him 120th, down from 72nd. I'd hold in 12-team 9-cat leagues for now since his shooting should improve, but he's not as bad as Mikal Bridges, who was near drop status.

    It has been revealed that gobert is 239th over the last two weeks and 289th over the last month. His rebound and block rates are both down: he's averaging 10.6 rebounds and 1.0 block in 29.2 minutes, compared to 11.5 and 1.6 last season. His scoring has dropped from 10.9 to 7.6 points, and his field goal percentage is down to 49% after he shot 68.2% last season. That FG% was the main reason to roster him in 9-cat. He's also shooting 46% from the line on 4.7 attempts per game. That's way too much volume for someone shooting so poorly.

    In a recent development, the former four-time defensive player of the year is more of a rebound specialist, so I'd look to move him if he can string together a few big double-double outings. I have him 150th, down from 110th. I'm probably still too generous.

    According to recent reports, reid has the volume in his first season in Charlotte: 17.7 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.5 3s in 31.5 minutes. The problem is efficiency. He's shooting 38% from the field on 17.5 attempts and 66% from the line, well below his career norms (45.6% and 73.2% last season in Minnesota), and he's adding 2.5 turnovers. That's why he's 149th over the last two weeks and 197th over the last month.

    It has been revealed that I have him 96th, down from 86th, because I expect his percentages to rebound once the Hornets get healthier and he isn't carrying as much of the offense. The volume makes him an easier hold in points leagues, but fantasy managers have every right to be concerned about his numbers.

    Julius Randle has brutal response to Nets' blowout loss: 'One of the worst games I've ever been a part of'

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a newly introduced low point.
    • The Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures.
    • The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a newly introduced low point.

    The Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest problem has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

    The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

    "I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35.

    "The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle stated after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable.".

    Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, New Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

    Recent findings suggest that there are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

    In a recent development, this early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

    Industry observers note that giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.

    #107802. NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1761 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1761 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects.
    • Industry observers note that in other areas, things are going … not so well.
    • According to recent reports, there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects. Luka Dončić and the Lakers are off to a hot start in Los Angeles. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs have picked up right where they left off after last season's Finals trip. And the Celtics are battling the new-look Sixers at the top of the Eastern Conference.

    Industry observers note that in other areas, things are going … not so well. Below are the eight biggest disappointments so far this season.

    According to recent reports, there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track. Jalen Duren (hamstring) has missed almost the entire season in Detroit. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from knee injuries and have yet to play for Golden State, while Steph Curry is now out with an abdominal tear and Kristaps Porziņģis stepped away from basketball. After sitting out all of last season with an Achilles tear, Tyrese Haliburton is at the moment dealing with a hamstring matter. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) hasn't made his debut for the Clippers. Austin Reaves is out with a heel injury. Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery and will miss a chunk of time for the Wolves, and it seems unlikely that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will play this season, even though he remains hopeful that he will. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with an ankle sprain. Ja Morant is out with a hamstring strain. Ben Simmons didn't play a single game for the Kings before tearing his Achilles. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is once again on the shelf in Toronto. And the reeling Jazz are without Jaren Jackson Jr (knee), Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe).

    It's all a huge bummer for the players, their teams and fans of hoops in general. But no team has been hurt more on the injury front than the Thunder.

    The disappointment here is how unkind fate has been to OKC. The Thunder were close to fully healthy when the season started — and then far from it not long after it began. When OKC beat the Spurs in San Antonio in the season opener — after losing four of five regular season games to them last season, as well as falling to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals — it felt like a statement that the Thunder were back and we were in for an epic battle between the two teams over who would rule the West.

    And then all of that was stripped away. Just three games into the season, Jalen Williams — who missed much of last season due to injury — suffered a gruesome fall and had to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula as well as reconstruction of ankle ligaments. In that same fateful game, Cason Wallace tore his labrum and later had shoulder surgery. They haven't been officially ruled out, but if either of them plays basketball again this season, it will be a surprise. Making matters worse, Chet Holmgren tore a tendon in his knee and "underwent a biological treatment" to address it. He'll miss approximately two months, but the Thunder do expect him to return. That's what passes for good news in OKC these days.

    Recent findings suggest that the Thunder are — or were — the deepest team in the NBA. That's a credit to what Sam Presti built. But even OKC has its limits. Losing three of five starters is tough to overcome, even when you're led by the reigning back-to-back MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That doesn't mean the Thunder (currently 9-6 and eighth in the West) can't still make a deep playoff run, but the odds of them doing so — and of them fighting the Spurs all season for the top spot — got a lot longer.

    In a recent development, we were told that this was finally the season that the East returned to its former glory. We were told that the conference would be loaded. We were wrong. (Full disclosure while putting a palm to my face: I might have done some of that telling.).

    Sources indicate that through the first month, the East has been mostly underwhelming. Eight of the 15 teams are below .500. The conference has a combined 17-37 record against the West. Only one of the top seven teams in net rating — the Celtics — plays in the East. Five of the top six teams by point differential play in the West.

    The defending champion Knicks are 8-6. The Cavaliers, who made it to last season's Eastern Conference Finals and had championship aspirations of their own, are 8-8. The Magic, Raptors and Pacers — who at the moment occupy the eight, nine and 10 seeds — all have losing records. By contrast, the worst play-in team in the West right now is Golden State at 8-7. That record would be good enough for the seven seed if they played in the East.

    Sources indicate that but maybe we shouldn't be surprised. Since the 1999-2000 season, the West has had the better overall record in all but three campaigns. Maybe next year the East will finally snap out of its funk, but don't bet on it.

    The Jazz just picked up back-to-back road wins in L.A. over the Lakers and Clippers, but that doesn't begin to dig them out of the deep hole they've made for themselves. The Jazz were gearing up to be competitive in the West this season. So much for that. Like the Thunder, injuries have not been kind to them. Nurkic has yet to play a single game this season, while Markkanen and JJJ have missed significant time with maladies of their own. What looked like a formidable frontcourt has been decimated.

    In a recent development, still, it's hard to believe how bad the Jazz have been in pretty much every facet. Their first win came in the second game of the season, a one-point squeaker over the Pelicans. It took until mid-November to end an ugly 12-game losing streak and pick up their second and third wins. They're 25th in net rating and point differential. The season has barely begun, and it's already basically wait until next year for the Jazz.

    Recent findings suggest that the NBA panicked and tried to solve for a problem that wasn't actually an issue, except for a small fragment of people who care more about optics than the product itself. And so the league enacted lottery reform and the upcoming 3-2-1 system was put in place. This was ostensibly designed to prevent tanking, incentivize winning and bring greater parity to the league. Oops.

    It has been revealed that the Hornets, Wizards, Bulls, Nets and Bucks are all well underwater in the East. The Pelicans and Clippers are drowning in the West, while the Kings and Jazz are even worse. What the league failed to account for is that some of these teams are just organically bad — and now they will have decreased odds at getting better.

    In a recent development, under the old system, the Grizzlies would be pretty thrilled to see the Jazz struggling since Memphis has Utah's first-round pick in the upcoming draft as part of the JJJ trade. Alas, after making that move, the league changed the rules, which means the Grizzlies can pick no higher than sixth now as a consequence of the new system preventing a team from picking in the top five in three consecutive drafts. Since the Jazz picked in the top five in each of the last two drafts, that means the Grizzlies are now out of luck with that Utah pick this time around. Womp, womp for them.

    And on top of it all, fans of bad teams were robbed of the entertaining-in-its-own-way race to the bottom to maximize lottery odds, giving supporters a small silver lining in the otherwise gray clouds of their season. RIP Tank Watch.

    Recent findings suggest that when aren't the Kings disappointing? Aside from their unsightly 1-13 record, the Sacramento front office continues to make baffling decisions. The Kings originally acquired Nique Clifford from the Thunder for a Spurs 2027 first-round pick. Sacramento held onto Clifford for 83 games — choosing to bury him on the bench this season and play him barely six minutes per game — before shipping him back to the Thunder for two second-round picks.

    So the Thunder ended up with the player and a first and the Kings ended up with two seconds.

    One of these organizations is savvy and opportunistic, and the other is the Kings. It's a miracle they nailed the Darius Acuff pick.

    According to recent reports, oof. It has not been a good season to date for Bridges. After going cold to begin their first-round playoff series against the Hawks, Bridges found his form and played well, helping the Knicks go on an epic run that ended with Fresh York's first championship in 53 years.

    Recent findings suggest that if that hope was that Bridges would snap out of his early-season funk in similar fashion, the Knicks seem somewhat less patient these days. While head coach Mike Brown has insisted that Bridges is a starter, he has sometimes hedged his bets in crucial situations, going with Landry Shamet or Deuce McBride over Bridges when things get tight and the Knicks need more reliable offense on the floor.

    Through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his fresh four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome.

    Sources indicate that why are we still subjected to … [motions at everything below in the most pejorative fashion possible] ... this?

    ALL 30 TEAM COURTS FOR @EMIRATES NBA CUP 2026 pic.twitter.com/RgBqe1VJCB.

    Why can't whoever came up with the gorgeous GTA VI crossover court in Miami be in charge of the Cup floors instead?

    The Miami Heat are rolling out the “Vice City” hardwood 😮‍💨👏(via @MiamiHEAT) pic.twitter.com/AFcyK2akaV.

    Sources indicate that respecting the Cup would be so much easier if they'd give us more of this. Maybe they could dream up some sweet upcoming jerseys while they're at it.

    Sonny Gray returns to Twins on two-year, $55 million contract, per report

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota.
    • Recent findings suggest that skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray!
    • According to recent reports, gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sonny Gray is heading back to Minnesota. The Twins on Wednesday revealed they have signed the veteran right-hander, who spent the 2022-23 seasons with the club. It's a two-year contract worth $55 million with an opt out, reports the Upcoming York Post.

    Recent findings suggest that skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny!Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57.

    According to recent reports, gray, 37, finished fifth in the American League Cy Young voting this season after throwing 169 innings with a 2.72 ERA and strong underlying numbers for the Boston Red Sox. He was the AL Cy Young runner-up in 2023, his final season with the Twins. All told, Gray threw 303 ⅔ innings with a 2.90 ERA during his time in Minnesota.

    CBS Sports ranked Gray as the No. 14 free agent available on the market this offseason. Here's our write-up:.

    Gray has reportedly mulled retirement over the last few offseasons, but he intends to pitch in 2027. He's as crafty as ever, using six pitches regularly and giving hitters every look. Hard, soft, sharp break, significant movement, etc. Gray's stuff works in such a way that he seems to get a quick first or second pitch out every inning, allowing him to pitch deep into games. He completed six innings 22 times in his 29 starts this past season, which makes him a workhorse by 2026 standards. Gray will pitch the entire 2027 season at age 37 and he's lost enough velocity to shrink his margin of error meaningfully, which creates some over-the-cliff risk. Still, the 14-year veteran is not out of place as the No. 2 starter in a postseason rotation.

    It has been revealed that gray now joins a Twins rotation that includes Taj Bradley, Joe Ryan and Pablo López, who missed last season after undergoing Tommy John surgery in February. Other options include Dean Kremer, Bailey Ober and Mick Abel.

    The Twins are coming off a 2026 season in which they went 77-85 with a -58 run differential. That landed them in third place in the American League Central and seven games out of the third and final wild-card spot in the AL. Although the Twins improved upon their 2025 record, they've now missed the postseason for three straight years, their longest drought in a decade. The Gray addition -- plus catcher Ryan Jeffers' acceptance of the qualifying offer for 2027 -- helps the cause, and no doubt the Twins under second-year manager Derek Shelton will be looking to get back to the playoffs in what again figures to be a winnable division.

    #107797. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5197 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
    • Recent findings suggest that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
    • Sources indicate that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

    Recent findings suggest that the narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct problems with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

    Sources indicate that all of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

    According to recent reports, A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

    In a recent development, joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Industry observers note that “It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

    Sources indicate that his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

    Industry observers note that maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

    Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

    Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc.

    In a recent development, marco Rose, their newly introduced manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he stated. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

    Industry observers note that his team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, newly introduced signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

    They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

    It has been revealed that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    Recent findings suggest that city will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “fresh Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

    There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

    Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a upcoming season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

    Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2.

    Recent findings suggest that the Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

    Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

    Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

    BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

    Recent findings suggest that maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

    Sources indicate that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

    Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

    Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

    Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

    City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

    Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

    No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6.

    Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

    Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

    Industry observers note that jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

    According to recent reports, foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

    According to recent reports, ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

    Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

    Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

    In a recent development, chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

    Recent findings suggest that villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

    Industry observers note that city are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

    Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

    Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

    Sources indicate that little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

    Recent findings suggest that anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

    Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

    Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

    In a recent development, highlights how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

    Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

    Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

    You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

    Sources indicate that "That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP.

    De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

    According to recent reports, villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

    Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

    We’re back under way at the Amex.

    Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

    Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four massive summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

    In a recent development, there’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

    A nightmare start for Emery’s side.

    There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

    #107795. Industry News: Rob Manfred 'can't imagine' MLB team owners will accept new CBA without a salary cap

    Industry News: Rob Manfred 'can't imagine' MLB team owners will accept new CBA without a salary cap

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday said club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a upcoming collective bargaining agreement.
    • "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred said while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in Fresh York, via the Athletic.
    • "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred said later during a news conference at MLB headquarters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday said club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a upcoming collective bargaining agreement. While Manfred noted there was general room for compromise with the MLBPA, that does not extend to the central matter of the capped system owners want.

    "I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred said while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in Fresh York, via the Athletic.

    "Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred said later during a news conference at MLB headquarters. "I'm not in a position to speculate about what happens in the event that we don't achieve our overriding objective, which is to get a cap and floor system that addresses the competitive problem that our fans perceive.".

    Industry observers note that it's possible to parse "can't imagine" as a subtle rhetorical hedge. Additionally, Manfred before he was commissioner was the league's lead negotiator. As such, he's quite familiar with the appearance of unyielding resolve as a tactical implement. Thus, the league has tied every other proposed change to the players' acceptance of a cap and floor, and the players through their union have historically shown zero willingness to accept such a system.

    "There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said Wednesday in a statement.

    It has been revealed that "There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.".

    Sources indicate that in their most recent substantive proposal to the players, MLB pitched a $258.3 million cap and $180.2 million floor on team payrolls, with those limits to be phased in gradually. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor.

    According to recent reports, the current CBA, which is the accord that governs every aspect of the working relationship between players and clubs in MLB, is set to expire just before midnight on Dec. 1. At that point, the league is expected to lock out the players at the behest of team owners. The lockout will likely not end until a new CBA is agreed to, at least in principle. Owners also locked out the players in 2021, and that lockout lasted 99 days and very nearly ate into the 2022 regular-season schedule.
