    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Newly introduced York Mets and center fielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year contract extension, SNY reports. The deal will pay Ewing a guaranteed $95 million and includes an option for a ninth year, according to The Athletic. The extension will run through the 2034 season and, if the option is exercised, through 2035.

    Industry observers note that ewing, 22, is coming off a 2026 rookie campaign in which he batted .252/.324/.376 (97 OPS+) with 11 home runs and 25 stolen bases in 120 games for the Mets. Additionally, Ewing graded out as a pronounced defensive asset in center field according to the eye test and fielding metrics. His overall WAR of 3.1 this past season helped him crack the top 10 in the National League Rookie of the Year vote.

    In a recent development, the Mets originally selected Ewing in the fourth round of the 2023 draft out of an Ohio high school. Following a strong campaign at Double-A and Triple-A in 2025, Ewing entered the 2026 season as a consensus top-100 prospect in baseball. In terms of overall value, he's already begun living up to those expectations.

    In a recent development, the extension expresses confidence on the club's side that Ewing will continue to be a valuable core contributor for years to come. Even if the bat doesn't develop as hoped, Ewing's foundation of excellent defense at an up-the-middle position provides him a high floor of worth over the long term. He's part of an emerging core of young Mets talent that also includes starting pitcher Nolan McLean and Ewing's fellow outfielder Carson Benge, who both finished ahead of Ewing in that Rookie of the Year balloting. As well, catcher Francisco Alvarez is still just 25 years old.

    No matter what happens with the Mets' high ambitions on the free-agent market, Ewing will be an essential part of the Mets' efforts to move beyond the disappointments of 2026. This past season, the Mets finished 14 games below .500 and in last place in the NL East despite having the league's highest Opening Day payroll.

    Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
    • Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
    • Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams revealed the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

    Sources indicate that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He noted at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

    Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

    After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, Latest Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

    RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Fresh Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

    Sources indicate that for the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a upcoming era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

    It has been revealed that goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a massive reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

    It has been revealed that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that Newly introduced Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

    Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

    Industry observers note that in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

    Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

    Sources indicate that in terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

    In a recent development, the most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

    Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Fresh Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

    Industry observers note that if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

    Sources indicate that let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

    Recent findings suggest that that said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

    Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

    Recent findings suggest that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

    Sources indicate that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

    Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

    According to recent reports, if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

    According to recent reports, the Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're in the throes of spooky season, and fittingly, the New Jersey Devils just got a lot scarier with the acquisition of superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.

    In a recent development, one of the best goaltenders in the world, Hellebuyck fills the biggest need on the Devils roster. With him in between the pipes and an electrifying group of forwards, Newly introduced Jersey will be a force in the Eastern Conference.

    Don't take my word for it. Just look at what the Devils did Tuesday against the Dallas Stars. In his first start with the team, Hellebuyck stopped 17 of the 18 shots he faced -- allowing one goal on 2.04 expected goals against -- in a 5-1 victory.

    It has been revealed that nico Hischier, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes each had multi-point nights as the Devils took full advantage of the chances they created against a stout Dallas team. This type of game has to be exactly what general manager Sunny Mehta envisioned when he swung the deal for Hellebuyck.

    Moving forward, the Devils will be burdened with the pressure that comes along with being a bona fide Cup contender. For a franchise that's fallen short of expectations a few times lately, that can be a scary prospect, and it inspired a special Halloween edition of the NHL Power Rankings in which I highlight the scariest thing about each team.

    Latest Update: NFL news, live updates: Steelers reportedly release Aaron Rodgers after he delivers rant on Mike McCarthy; 49ers QB Brock Purdy dealing with ankle injury

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Week 12 of the NFL season kicks off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.
    • Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.
    • Recent findings suggest that this storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 12 of the NFL season kicks off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

    Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

    Recent findings suggest that this storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers.".

    Shortly after his appearance on the show, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that Rodgers was being released. The quarterback had remarked on the show that he was "not going back to Pittsburgh.".

    We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have already ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for his third consecutive game with a groin injury, giving rookie Emmett Johnson the nod for a Thanksgiving contest with the Buffalo Bills.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

    The Jaguars were without running back Bhayshul Tuten at Wednesday's practice as he deals with both a foot and ankle injury.

    With the chaotic week, Jacksonville benefits from a normal schedule, not having to play the Titans until Sunday.

    Recent findings suggest that tuten has played in all 10 games for Jacksonville this season. He has 642 yards and five touchdowns on 158 carries, and has added an additional 226 yards and three more scores on 21 receptions.

    San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters on Wednesday.

    Shanahan specified that Purdy does not have a high-ankle injury, but the quarterback may not be able to play Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.

    If Purdy can't start the NFC West divisional game, backup quarterback Mac Jones is expected to take over.

    San Francisco is 9-1 and leads both the division and the NFC. The 49ers had their bye week in Week 8 and have won three consecutive games.

    Recent findings suggest that purdy is having one of the best seasons of his career. In just 10 games, he has already thrown more touchdowns (23) than in each of his last two seasons (20). Purdy has thrown for 2,624 yards and five interceptions, and has added 222 additional yards and two more scores on the ground.

    While the Rams continue taking injury hits on offense, they are getting a reinforcement on defense.

    Defensive end Kobie Turner has been activated ahead of Wednesday night's game against the Packers.

    According to recent reports, turner had been on IR because of a groin injury and last played on October 18. He heads into tonight's game with just seven sacks on the year.

    The Steelers have reportedly released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers, per Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac.

    Rodgers' release was reportedly expedited after the quarterback went scorched-earth on former head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show.".

    The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday.

    Recent findings suggest that the schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway.

    Industry observers note that there's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most vital games, in terms of what's at stake.

    Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.

    Aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

    The Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the New York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

    This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the new deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

    Read more on Aiyuk's recent signing.

    In a recent development, the Chiefs are looking at another game without star running back Kenneth Walker III. Despite returning to practice Tuesday, Walker will reportedly not play against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, according to multiple reports.

    It will mark the third straight game Walker will miss due to the concern.

    Recent findings suggest that prior to the injury, Walker was well on his way toward posting his finest season in the NFL. Through eight games, the running back already rushed for 872 yards and seven touchdowns. He also hauled in 26 catches for 172 yards and four receiving scores.

    There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

    It's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he mentioned will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

    It has been revealed that it was still abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

    It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

    The Steelers made the decision late Tuesday night to bench quarterback Aaron Rodgers. On Wednesday morning, the team began dealing with the fallout from that decision.

    Sources indicate that rodgers was reportedly not in the building early Wednesday when the Steelers held their morning team meeting at 8 a.m. ET, per ESPN's Brooke Pryor.

    Additional reporting suggested Rodgers was excused from going to team facilities the day after it was unveiled he was benched.

    At that meeting, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy officially announced the quarterback change to the rest of the team. That decision was reportedly "not a popular" one within the locker room, per The Athletic.

    While Rodgers struggled this season, he was still well-liked by his teammates, per Pryor.

    The Pittsburgh Steelers announced Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

    Aaron Rodgers will be inactive.

    The Eagles listed star running back Saquon Barkley as a full practice participant on Tuesday.

    The injury report did note that it was just a walkthrough, but yesterday, when Philly did not practice, the team listed Barkley as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury as well as an illness.

    The Eagles play the Cowboys on Thursday afternoon for Thanksgiving.

    Brandon Aiyuk may have a newly introduced home sooner than later.

    Industry observers note that the former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

    Ayiuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after previously being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise.

    After finally being released by the San Francisco 49ers, veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has cleared waivers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, who also reported Tuesday that Aiyuk would like to sign with a upcoming team soon.

    He's expected to attract interest from a few teams, including the Washington Commanders, per Schefter.

    The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 NFL season after recovering from a knee injury he suffered in 2024, just months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the team. He suffered a torn ACL and MCL in late October 2024 and hasn't played a snap in the league since.

    Industry observers note that san Francisco had a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk. It expired on Monday, and as a result, the franchise opted to release Aiyuk, giving both the team and the wide receiver a fresh start.

    According to recent reports, denver Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins has been suspended for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, according to head coach Sean Payton.

    Payton did not get into specifics and told reporters he would not comment further on the situation.

    Recent findings suggest that dobbins, 27, is in his second season with the Broncos. He has rushed for 324 yards and 3 touchdowns on 99 carries, adding 31 receiving yards on 9 catches. Last year, Dobbins compiled 772 rushing yards and 4 TDs.

    Industry observers note that the suspension leaves Denver will be without its leading rusher for Friday's Week 12 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jonah Coleman (302 rushing yards in 6 games) will presumably take over as the starter.

    Micah Parsons is officially activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list, Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst announced on Tuesday.

    So the All-Pro pass rusher appears to be ready to play in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons had been listed as questionable for the game.

    Parsons has been sidelined while recovering from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered during Week 15 last season. Prior to his injury, he compiled 12.5 sacks in 14 games (13 starts) in his first year with Green Bay.

    While Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is reportedly poised to make his long-awaited return from his ACL injury Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, he's officially listed as "questionable" for the Week 12 matchup.

    In Parsons' first, abridged season with the Packers, he piled up 12.5 sacks over 14 games.

    Running back Josh Jacobs is also "questionable" for the Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

    He's been recovering from surgery on the ring finger he fractured.

    The Kansas City Chiefs have been cautious handling the groin injury that running back Kenneth Walker III is navigating.

    Walker hasn't played since Nov. 8, a Week 9 win over the New York Jets.

    Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters that Walker will return to practice Tuesday.

    Recent findings suggest that "We'll see how he does," Reid said, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work there, but he'll get out there and move around.".

    The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo this week for a Thanksgiving showdown with the Bills.

    If there's anything that can slow this 49ers team, it's the blue medical tent. Injuries have ravaged the 49ers all season, and on Sunday night, San Francisco ran out a Geriatric Avengers of thirty-somethings including George Kittle, Mike Evans, Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Kyle Juszczyk. All that experience gives the 49ers a massive-game-pressure edge that few teams can match, but it also makes them intensely vulnerable to injury. Stints on the IR are a when, not an if, for the 49ers. Right tackle Colton McKivitz was the latest as he suffered a gruesome leg injury in the first half Sunday night.

    Industry observers note that the guy ensuring all those uncs get the ball is finally receiving some attention of his own again, too. Brock Purdy hasn't shown up on MVP leaderboards since finishing fourth in his breakout season of 2023. This season ought to change that. He's among the league leaders in touchdowns, passer rating and completion percentage, among other useful stats.

    According to recent reports, against the best defense in the NFL, all Purdy did was throw for three touchdowns and 255 yards on 21-of-26 completions. He's grown into the perfect weapon for head coach Kyle Shanahan's unorthodox offense, and Sunday was the perfect showcase.

    McCarthy was asked on Monday whether he was considering a quarterback change after the offense's poor play in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

    McCarthy kept it short and to the point, saying, "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback.".

    Pittsburgh dropped to 6-4 after the loss and fell to third place in the AFC North, trailing both the Cincinnati Bengals and the Cleveland Browns.

    Industry observers note that the Steelers had 255 yards of offense but couldn't beat the Eagles. Philadelphia's win ended a seven-game losing streak for the franchise, and the Steelers have now lost two straight games, both coming after their Week 9 bye.

    In a recent development, in the loss, Rodgers was 30-of-44 passing for 227 yards and a touchdown. He led the team in rushing with 29 yards on five carries, but was sacked five times.

    If the New England Patriots are interested in adding quarterback Daniel Jones, head coach Mike Vrabel isn't saying so.

    While Jones has cleared waivers, the Patriots named Tommy DeVito as their starting QB for Week 12's matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers. However, even if New England signed Jones, he would be unlikely to take the field with them so soon after joining the team.

    According to recent reports, taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel stated he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

    The NBA season started one month ago today. The first stanza of the campaign brought a great deal of excitement at the top of the league with superstars doing superstar things and most of the projected championship contenders getting off to hot starts. But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.

    Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season. Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player:.

    Recent findings suggest that another major disappointment: The Kings. How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams.

    In a recent development, the College Football Selection Committee is in love with the SEC. Only one time in three different rankings have the bracket-makers ranked a team from that conference lower than AP Top 25 voters. Whether or not you think it's fair, the numbers largely back it up. In fact, two-loss No. 5 Texas even has a better resume score than undefeated No. 2 Utah! So maybe the committee is not all that out of line. You can be sure they will have their eyes on these five key matchups in Week 12.

    Another vital clash is the only top-25 contest of the week: No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina. In his Six Pack of picks, our Tom Fornelli explained why the Bulldogs will roll on the road.

    It has been revealed that moving away from the SEC, look out for a potential upset in the Big Ten. Nothing is going well for Michigan, but the Wolverines are only small underdogs against unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. These five factors will determine whether the Bruins move one step closer to the CFP or fall for the first time this season.

    Here's how to watch the biggest games of Week 12 and our picks for each of them:.

    Industry observers note that this is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. The Bears and Broncos are also favored by double digits. The Cowboys, Lions, Jaguars and Bengals are all favored by about a touchdown. You know how these things go, though. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert, and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.

    Industry observers note that first of all, the Buccaneers have just as much to play for as the Lions. Both of them are locked into tightly contested division battles. The motivation will be there for a Tampa Bay team that could somehow sneak into the playoffs even with a losing record. And then there's the Tampa Bay defense, which has forced at least four turnovers in each of its last three games. Our Tyler Sullivan mentioned it would not surprise him if Jared Goff's interception streak continues.

    And even though our Jordan Dajani could not bring himself to pick the upset outright, he does see the Buccaneers keeping this one highly competitive.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below.

    Industry observers note that will the San Francisco Giants trade their ace this offseason? That's a reasonable question to ask now that FanSided is reporting that the Giants are open to trade discussions regarding veteran right-hander Logan Webb. No doubt, Webb would be a coveted presence on the offseason market.

    Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top-10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings.

    Webb is under contract through 2028, and that extra year of team control makes him even more of an alluring trade target for contenders in need of rotation upgrades.

    Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports.

    Industry observers note that peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the New York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form.

    Sources indicate that right-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front.

    In a recent development, the 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons.     📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1555 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Aaron Rodgers became the NFL's rebel, and his scorched-earth interview was a fitting end in Pittsburgh

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Near the end of an instantly legendary interview, which will be remembered for years and years to come, Aaron Rodgers felt the need to explain why he just had aired out Mike McCarthy in a way that a player has never quite ripped his coach before.
    • The way Rodgers delivered the message on "The Pat McAfee Show" was almost as startling as the accusations themselves.
    • He then needed to tell everyone why he was spilling all the embarrassing stories, or more specifically, why he didn't care about the fallout.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Near the end of an instantly legendary interview, which will be remembered for years and years to come, Aaron Rodgers felt the need to explain why he just had aired out Mike McCarthy in a way that a player has never quite ripped his coach before.

    The way Rodgers delivered the message on "The Pat McAfee Show" was almost as startling as the accusations themselves. He said McCarthy would sleep in meetings and miss practices. That he didn't bother to get to know some Steelers defensive stars like Cameron Heyward and T.J. Watt at all. And Rodgers told it all without ever getting emotional. He rarely changed his matter-of-fact tone over the more than 30 minutes the interview lasted.

    He then needed to tell everyone why he was spilling all the embarrassing stories, or more specifically, why he didn't care about the fallout.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's going to be hard for [other Steelers teammates] to tell the truth, like I can," Rodgers told McAfee. "I can, because what are the repercussions for me? I don't care about getting released. I don't care about making any more money. I don't care how this is viewed by the same people who railed me for COVID who already have their opinions about me. I'm standing on the truth. That's why it's not emotional for me anymore.".

    Recent findings suggest that everyone already knew that, at the age of 42, Rodgers didn't really care what people thought of him anymore. Multiple interviews on multiple topics late in his career are proof of that. And there should certainly be skepticism over what the truth actually is. Disgruntled parties can twist stories to fit self-serving narratives , and Rodgers had just been benched for the first time in his 22-year NFL career. He was released not long after the McAfee interview, which was no surprise to anyone who heard it.

    The nuance of what Rodgers stated doesn't matter much to this larger point: The defiant reputation Rodgers grew late in his career was always going to lead to a moment like this, which has never really been seen in the NFL before.

    Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, second from left, and Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers had a contentious meeting on Tuesday according to Rodgers. (AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar).

    Sources indicate that when word started getting around that Rodgers was going on McAfee's ESPN show at about 1:40 p.m. Eastern time, it was time to tune in. There was no chance that Rodgers was going to go on a show that he has been on many times before and acquiesce. Everyone knew he was incapable of going out quietly. And he didn't.

    Industry observers note that even with that as a backdrop, it was shocking. Many things that happen in a meeting or locker room do not get shared with the public. Rodgers revealed it all, or at least his version of it.

    Sources indicate that rodgers said he found out he was benched when tight end Pat Freiermuth called him incredulous about the news Rodgers hadn't heard yet. That ended up being one of the tamer revelations of the interview with McAfee.

    Rodgers said that last week, McCarthy fell asleep twice in a quarterback meeting on Wednesday. Rodgers said McCarthy also missed an offensive meeting and a walkthrough on Thursday, then missed another walkthrough on Friday and missed a morning meeting on Saturday. There was no team meeting "for whatever reason" on Saturday night, Rodgers said.

    In a recent development, "Last Wednesday we were in a quarterback meeting, Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers mentioned. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around, five minutes later you heard the snoring again.".

    Rodgers wouldn't stop. He said McCarthy told him on Tuesday that he was behind in watching film on the Broncos, who the Steelers play on Sunday.

    In a recent development, "He just states, this is Tuesday by the way, three days from playing, he says "I'm a little behind on film, I've just seen clips at this point,'" Rodgers stated. "There's already a first and second, third down install in at this point. That's when I'm like, what are we doing?".

    He said it was common for McCarthy to tell him he had not watched film.

    Recent findings suggest that "I don't think he knows the plan. I think he learns the plan during the week," Rodgers told McAfee. "Multiple times he mentioned he doesn't watch film, when I've talked to him on Tuesdays, he hasn't seen the film yet. I don't know how that's possible, on a Tuesday after you play on a Sunday. That's the whole point. That part is disrespectful to the game itself, but you have peoples' careers involved.".

    Rodgers said the concerns had been going on for weeks in Pittsburgh, and years before that when the two were together with the Green Bay Packers. He went so far as to take responsibility for suggesting to the Steelers that McCarthy should get an interview after Mike Tomlin stepped down as head coach, because he knew McCarthy's habits. Rodgers went back years, talking about similar situations with the Packers, particularly after an NFC championship game loss at Seattle at the end of the 2014 season in which he confronted McCarthy about his "habits that week" including missing multiple walkthroughs and meetings.

    Story after story came from Rodgers, who offered them up with the same amount of emotion as if he was reading a grocery list.

    It has been revealed that "I've sat on this for a long time," Rodgers noted. "I sat on it for 10 years, 10 years in Green Bay with this stuff going on, 10 years that I was aware of. But we worked around it. We won division championships, went to the playoffs eight straight years. It's like, is there a better way to do this? Is there a world where this doesn't exist like this? It's on me, because I vouched for him, and I thought it would be different.".

    Many things have and will be said about Rodgers, but it's also true to say that no other player would have given an interview quite like that one.

    According to recent reports, the beginning of the end of Rodgers' time in Pittsburgh came when he went to McCarthy with what he called an ultimatum. McCarthy should give up play-calling, or release him.

    It has been revealed that "It wasn't a veiled ultimatum," Rodger said. "It wasn't posturing.".

    According to recent reports, the end of his time with the Steelers officially came shortly after an interview that will be infamous in NFL circles. If Rodgers was angling to get released and perhaps finish what he said will be his final season starting somewhere else, he knew how to do it.

    There haven't been many NFL situations to play out this way in the public realm. Rodgers' interview that led to his release will go alongside Terrell Owens doing pushups in his driveway, Antonio Brown quitting on the Buccaneers and running back to the locker room in the middle of a game or any other infamous moments that won't be forgotten. There's a code that many of the things Rodgers shared aren't to be repeated in the media. He clearly didn't care because he shared it all, or at least his version of what happened.

    There will be a fallout from it as Rodgers walks away from the fire he set. McCarthy's reputation will be hard to repair after this, and perhaps that was Rodgers' goal after being benched in an unceremonious way near the end of what he remarked will be his final season. Perhaps players will leak confirmation to Rodgers' stories anonymously, but not many people are willing to speak poorly about their boss. But it will all linger over the Steelers as long as McCarthy is coaching there.

    Recent findings suggest that rodgers didn't care. The breaking point for him, he said, came at halftime of last week's loss at Philadelphia when McCarthy brought the team together and broke them down with a "1, 2, 3, Packers!" McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018.

    According to recent reports, "Eight years removed, with a team in between," Rodgers said. "And a game we needed to win to get to 7-3.".

    The breaking point for McCarthy and the Steelers might have been that he shared that story at all.

    From the outside looking in, it had been a fun reunion between Rodgers and McCarthy, at least before this week. The Steelers had lost two in a row, but at 6-4 they are still in the playoff field. That's not what we'll remember. We'll remember the unbelievable way it all ended in a public manner over a period of about 14 hours.

    Industry observers note that "It had a chance, it really did," Rodgers said. "It had a good chance to be one of those really cool stories.".

    It did end up being a heck of a story, and while it would be cliche to say this is all not the story Rodgers wanted, that's only partially true. Given Rodgers' rebellious and outspoken ways the past few years, it almost certainly had to end like this.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Sources indicate that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Sources indicate that kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Sources indicate that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    According to recent reports, it's notable to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    It has been revealed that we already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    Industry observers note that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Industry observers note that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It has been revealed that it was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
    • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
    • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    Industry observers note that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    Recent findings suggest that forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

    In a recent development, newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    According to recent reports, speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    In a recent development, of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    "There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

    "It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels.     Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

    The substantial breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

    Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

    It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

    Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s latest head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    It has been revealed that daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

    Aaron Rodgers rips Mike McCarthy, says Steelers coach fell asleep in meeting and mistakenly called team 'Packers'; other players reportedly corroborate quarterback's account

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not stay silent for long following his surprise benching.
    • Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, joined the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon to address his benching … and he did not hold back when it came to sharing his side of how the events of the week unfolded — or when it comes to his feelings about McCarthy.
    • Recent findings suggest that "I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said in the interview.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers did not stay silent for long following his surprise benching. And shortly after Rodgers publicly accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of everything from sleeping in meetings to mistakenly calling the team the "Packers," the franchise reportedly decided to release the veteran quarterback.

    Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, joined the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon to address his benching … and he did not hold back when it came to sharing his side of how the events of the week unfolded — or when it comes to his feelings about McCarthy.

    Recent findings suggest that "I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth," Rodgers said in the interview. "I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, 'I can't believe they're doing this.' And I said, 'Doing what?' I didn't know. And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn't hear from Mike [McCarthy].".

    "Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up," Rodgers continued.

    After that, Rodgers released a windfall of scathing accusations against McCarthy, ripping into his head coach for a series of events over the past week that "ultimately led to where we're at now.".

    Rodgers remarked McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks meeting last Wednesday, in which the coach fell asleep and was snoring.

    It has been revealed that "Last Wednesday, we're in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rogers stated. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.".

    Rodgers accused McCarthy of missing an offensive meeting the following day and also missed the Friday walkthrough.

    "Doesn't come to the first walkthrough," Rodgers said. "Doesn't come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn't great.".

    Rodgers also ripped into McCarthy's relationships with players on the team, alleging that he didn't care to get to know the defense and had lost many of those players well before the end.

    Sources indicate that "There were some guys early on that were … didn't like the way things were going, especially defensive guys. Mike didn't want to get to know the defense," Rodgers said. "At one point, I told him, 'You should really lean into the defensive guys a little bit more and talk to those guys,' and he said, 'Well, I don't think I need to.' And I said, 'Well, I disagree with that.'".

    "He already kind of lost a lot of those guys, and I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was, at halftime, toward the end of it … he says, 'Alright, 1-2-3-Packers!' That's what he broke it down on in the locker room," Rodgers said. "We all looked around, going, 'What the f***? What is going on? Where's his head at, at this point?".

    The Steelers went on to lose that game, 19-16, snapping a seven-game losing streak for the Philadelphia Eagles. Rodgers took five sacks in the loss, completing 30-of-44 pass attempts for 227 yards and a score.

    Clearly, the loss was a tipping point for Rodgers.

    Recent findings suggest that "I went in on Monday, and I just said, "Hey, this last week, this is not what we talked about. We've had these conversations for months now. And it began as a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy. If you're not coming to everything you should be coming to as a playcaller, [you're unhealthy].

    It has been revealed that "I mean, how many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff? I gave you one week. I could go week-by-week throughout the season on stuff that was going on.

    "Monday, we're having this conversation, and I said, 'We need to make a change for the betterment of the team.'".

    Sources indicate that the change Rodgers was hoping for was a change in playcaller. But instead, the team made a change at quarterback.

    Sources indicate that "I felt like I was talking to him at the behest of the team," Rogers said. "It was pretty wild. I'm saying these things to him that I told you. He's denying all of it. He's denying sleeping. I go, 'Mike, there's five guys in the room that would sign an affidavit.' There's no hyperbole. There's no trying to stick it you. What's best for the team is you give [play calling] up to somebody, you take of yourself, you take care of your health, do the schedule and do the team meetings and let that be that.".

    Industry observers note that "When I talk to him on Tuesdays, he states I haven't seen the film yet, I haven't seen the film." Rodgers noted. "I don't know how that's possible on Tuesday when you play on a Sunday. That part's disrespectful to the game. You have peoples' livelihoods involved, players and coaches.".

    "I left it with him that if you try and bench me or don't change the play-calling, then you should just release me because I feel like at this point I'm doing what's right for the organization," Rogers said. "He responded with, 'I'm going to do what's right for the organization,' and, in his mind, that's getting rid of me.".

    How do Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers move forward after this?

    Well … apparently, they don't. Rodgers acknowledged as much nearing the end of his McAfee appearance, saying the "ship has sailed" on a return to the team. Soon after Rodgers' interview concluded, it was reported that the Steelers were releasing Rodgers, according to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette beat writer Gerry Dulac. Other reports have since confirmed the same.

    The real question now is how the Steelers will move forward with McCarthy, after multiple league sources have corroborated Rodgers' account to ESPN.

    We're just over one month into the season, and the Pittsburgh Penguins are three games below .500 and 15th in the Eastern Conference. This slow start could create some very tough decisions for general manager Kyle Dubas.

    On the heels of a resurgence in 2025-26, the Penguins haven't quite been able to recapture that magic yet, and there's a good chance Father Time has something to do with that. The core of this team is one of the oldest in the NHL, and not even Sidney Crosby can remain an elite superstar forever.

    Recent findings suggest that if the Penguins continue to occupy the bottom of the Eastern Conference, Dubas will face tough decisions. He has a handful of stars on expiring or soon-to-be-expiring contracts, and those players could be very attractive to other teams. Erik Karlsson seems like and obvious trade candidate. As does Rickard Rakell.

    But if there was a fire sale, would Dubas go as far as shipping out a franchise icon?

    Industry observers note that look, it's still very early, and there are reasons to believe a turnaround is coming. The Penguins' five-on-five numbers are far better than the results indicate, and Crosby is fully capable of shaking off a slow start and hitting another level.

    If things don't improve, though, things could get very interesting in Pittsburgh. As the Pens sink, here are the updated NHL Power Rankings.

    Latest Update: Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways

    • It has been revealed that let's set the stage here.
    • It has been revealed that did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan debuted himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    It has been revealed that let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    It has been revealed that did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Sources indicate that officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    Recent findings suggest that that begs an crucial question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    Industry observers note that wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    Fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he noted after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.
